prompt: Work out an order in which a set of classes can be compiled, or report that their dependencies form a cycle. Complete CompileOrderPlanner and run the tests.
explanation: This is a topological sort: keep a set of classes whose dependencies are all satisfied, place one, and re-check whoever was waiting on it. Storing the ready classes in a TreeSet makes pollFirst hand back the alphabetically smallest one, which is what keeps the answer deterministic. If the loop stops before every class has been placed, the classes left over are all waiting on each other -- that is exactly a cycle, so returning an empty list doubles as the cycle report.
hints: First build a map from each class to the set of dependencies that are keys of the input map; ignore names that are not keys.
Keep the classes whose dependency set is empty in a TreeSet and use pollFirst() so ties are broken alphabetically.
After placing a class, remove it from everyone else's set; anyone whose set just became empty joins the ready set. If you placed fewer classes than the map holds, there is a cycle.
